newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Bunds target 99.79 but upside limited.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Bunds target 99.79 but upside limited.

text.p: June Bund futures on LIFFE on Wednesday will attempt to fill a gap from last week's close of 99.79 as the German market is encouraged by firmer U.S. Treasuries, but the upside is limited, analysts said.
"What we saw yesterday was a new test of very significant support around 99.28," said ABN-AMRO Hoare Govett technical analyst Geert-Jan Nikken in Amsterdam.
"For the moment it seems that support holds," he said. "What we are facing now is only slightly higher prices."
June Bunds at 0652 GMT were at 99.70, up 0.26. They had left a gap from Thursday's 99.79 low to Tuesday's 99.70 high.
Nikken said if the market filled that gap there were new selling opportunities, with good resistance at 99.85 to offer another stumbling block.
John Ratcliffe, senior money market analyst at Technical Data in London, agreed that 99.79 was the initial goal.
"It's got a bit more upside," he said. He said a steep downtrend since late February comes in around 100.00.
He did not see that level as a serious obstacle but rather as a potentiallly positive indicator if the market got above it.
"But I have to see prices well above par before I turn bullish," he added.
"I certainly can't get too enthursed about the whole thing until 100.54 gets exceeded," Ratcliffe said, noting a March 26 high.
Nikken said there was scope for a new attempt on Tuesday's important 99.26-28 floor.

"However we will find some support at 99.52," he said, noting that was a low on March 20 and also a level where the market found resistance on hourly charts during its bounce on Tuesday. Ratcliffe said he would not get immediately bearish unless the market went below Tuesday's lows.
